key_insight: For tabular foundation models, the biggest inference efficiency gains come from quantizing the attention computation itself, rather than focusing mainly on weight or KV-cache quantization as is common in LLMs. The paper argues that query/key/value quantization is the right lever for these models.
problem_solved: Tabular foundation models are increasingly used in inference settings, but serving them efficiently is challenging. Existing LLM-style optimization priorities do not transfer well, so the paper addresses how to reduce inference cost for tabular models in a way that matches their architecture and usage patterns.
method: Analyze where inference bottlenecks actually occur in tabular foundation models.
Shift quantization focus from weights/KV cache to the attention mechanism.
Develop a quantization strategy for queries, keys, and values to improve efficiency while preserving model performance.
impact: This helps practitioners deploy tabular foundation models faster and more cheaply, especially in latency- or throughput-sensitive settings. It also provides a clearer optimization target for efficiency research beyond LLM-centric assumptions.
visual_elements: Attention block diagram highlighting Q/K/V quantization points
Before-vs-after inference pipeline showing reduced compute cost
Comparison chart of quantization targets: weights vs KV cache vs attention
Simple icon set for speed, memory, and accuracy trade-offs
paper_title: Attention Quantization for Tabular Foundation Models
paper_authors: Jonas M. Kübler, Benjamin Jäger, Klemens Flöge, Noah Hollmann, Frank Hutter
